page: Microsoft Azure DC96es_v6 is a general-purpose confidential computing virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon processor featuring Intel TDX hardware architecture. The instance provides 96 vCPUs spanning 48 physical cores with two threads per core, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes hardware acceleration for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX for deep learning matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel execution capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the DC96es_v6 scores in the top 25% for multi-core processing with 77,153.44 points, contrasting with an average mid-tier single-core score of 1,765.59. Furthermore, in-memory throughput is demonstrated by Redis SET performance measuring 93.52 million operations per second, ranking within the top quartile of tested instances.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external attached volumes such as Azure Premium Storage. The high core count and dense memory configuration offer solid qualitative resource efficiency for parallelized processing without the infrastructure overhead of discrete accelerators.

Given its hardware profile and confidential computing capabilities, the DC96es_v6 is well matched for scalable backend infrastructure, distributed in-memory data stores, enterprise microservices, encrypted database workloads, and compute-intensive batch processing pipelines.

Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it supplies 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 384.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU allocation. The CPU incorporates advanced vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX, and accelerated cryptographic modules. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and in-memory execution, scoring 77,153.44 on multi-core stress-ng tests and achieving 93.52 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, both ranking in the top 25%. Without bundled local storage or GPUs, it utilizes remote network storage options. The instance is suited for enterprise application hosting, confidential transactional databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput multi-threaded workloads.
